item.content: {"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=epistemic+frameworks+for+autonomous+agent+evaluation+of+human-provided+objectives+and+goal-alignment+verification&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.7427298\", \"title\": [\"Autonomous Micro-Enterprise Governance (AMEG): Architectural Accountability, Deontic-Epistemic Verification, and Statutory Auditability in Multi-Agent Systems\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>As autonomous multi-agent generative systems transition from conversational prototypes to high-stakes revenue-bearing infrastructure, organizational accountability can no longer rely on extrinsic policy documents audited ex-post. This paper formalizes Autonomous Micro-Enterprise Governance, an architectural runtime framework that embeds institutional governance and statutory mandates directly into the state-transition dynamics of autonomous firms. \\n<br>\\n<br>\\n Extending the Autonomous Micro-Enterprise Architecture state-machine model, it establishes an institutionally regulated eight-tuple combining state spaces, agent actions, transition functions, environmental streams, deontic constraint lattices, settlement primitives, epistemic registries, and execution ledgers. Institutional policies are formalized as a dynamic deontic constraint lattice of obligations, permissions, and prohibitions combined with multi-agent epistemic state tracking, evaluated via a deterministic validation predicate prior to external settlement dispatch. \\n<br>\\n<br>\\n To operationalize the EU AI Act, specifically Title III requirements for high-risk systems under Articles 9, 11, 12, 14, and 15, discrete state mutations are recorded in a cryptographic, tamper-evident Merkle execution tree, guaranteeing mathematical auditability and causal traceability without persisting unbounded natural-language logs. We prove that under a sound normative lattice and bounded self-correction refinement, the probability of an uncontained statutory violation reaching external settlement is analytically bounded. We demonstrate that this framework decouples compliance enforcement from human monitoring payroll while preserving jurisdictional portability across emerging global frameworks.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10…
